title: Counter decrement and tape preservation
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ and $\Gamma$ be types with decidable equality, let $e$ be an embedding of the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape machine over $\Gamma$ with state set $S$. Choose a designated state $a\in S$, an optional exit state, a configuration $c$ on input $x$, a Boolean word $w$, and a counter tape $ct:\mathbb{Z}\to\operatorname{Option}(\Gamma)$ whose head is at $cp\in\mathbb{Z}$. Assume that for every integer $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, the content of $ct$ at $cp+p$ equals the content at $p$ of the buffer storing the word obtained by applying $e$ to each symbol of $w$. Let $r$ be the number of initial false symbols of $w$, and let $v$ be the fixed-length decrement of $w$, with the all-true word of length $|w|$ used if that decrement is undefined. After $2r+2$ steps of the counter-loop machine, started from the decrement phase with configuration $c$ and counter tape $ct$, the configuration is the one with state equal to the body state at $a$ if the decrement is defined and the finished state otherwise; its first $k$ work tapes and head positions are those of $c$, and its counter tape is $ct$ patched on the interval from $cp$ through $cp+|w|-1$ with the buffer storing the image of $v$ under $e$. At every earlier time, the machine is neither finished nor escaped; through time $2r+2$, the counter head stays in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and the first $k$ work-head positions remain those of $c$.
